note: Mar Zutra visited Rav Ashi's home, and they offered him food. They set meat before him, saying: Eat, Master, it is especially healthful, because it is a firstborn. He asked where it came from, and they said a certain priest had sold it to them. Mar Zutra asked whether they did not hold, with Rav Huna son of Rabbi Yehoshua, that this looks like a priest helping at the threshing floor; they said no, since they had bought it. He pressed them with a mishna that forbids handing a firstborn to a priest early for the same reason. They replied that there the favor is plain to see, while here they had simply bought it.
why: Rav Huna son of Rabbi Yehoshua has just explained that a priest may not sell an unblemished firstborn to an Israelite, because it looks like a discount in exchange for future gifts. This incident tests that rule against a sale at fair market value.

people.name: Mar Zutra
people.about: A guest at Rav Ashi's home who questions the firstborn meat served to him.

people.name: Rav Huna son of Rabbi Yehoshua
people.about: The Sage whose rule Mar Zutra cites.

people.name: Rav Sheshet
people.about: Gives the reason behind the mishna Mar Zutra quotes.

terms.meaning: The firstborn male of a cow, sheep or goat is holy and belongs to a priest. Unblemished, it is offered on the altar; an ordinary Israelite may eat one only if it has a blemish.

terms.term: a priest who assists at the threshing floor
terms.meaning: A priest who helps a farmer at harvest so the farmer will give him his priestly gifts. The Sages forbade anything that looks like trading favors for those gifts.
